subject: How can I evaluate the model performance?

messages.author: 82a29501c95feac5
messages.subject: How can I evaluate the model performance?
parts:
Hi all,

I want to know how can I evaluate the performance of the model and the significance of covariates in INLA (y ~ 1 + b0 + x1 + x2)? Specifically, can I calculate the BIC criterion or something like p-value in INLA? Thank you.

Best,
Kuan

messages.author: 74f2e6fef4c447fd
messages.subject: Re: How can I evaluate the model performance?
parts:
Hi Kuan,

Here is some code that shows common model and variable evaluation methods.

Best,
Tim

# data
n <- 50; a <- 40; b <- -1.5; sigma2 <- 50; x1 <- 1:n
x2 <- sample(1:n); g1 <- sample(gl(5, 10))
eps <- rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd=sqrt(sigma2))
y <- a + b*x1 + eps; hist(y)
plot(x1, y)
plot(x2, y)
plot(g1, y)

# run competing models
library(INLA)
library(brinla) # for evaluating random effects
dat <- data.frame(y, x1, x2, g1)
r0 <- inla(y ~ 1, data=dat, family="gaussian",
           control.compute=list(cpo=T, waic=T, dic=T, config=T))
r1 <- inla(y ~ 1 + x1, data=dat, family="gaussian",
           control.compute=list(cpo=T, waic=T, dic=T, config=T))
r2 <- inla(y ~ 1 + x1 + x2, data=dat, family="gaussian",
           control.compute=list(cpo=T, waic=T, dic=T, config=T))
r3 <- inla(y ~ 1 + x1 + x2 + f(g1, model="iid"), data=dat, family="gaussian",
           control.compute=list(cpo=T, waic=T, dic=T, config=T))

# compare models with information criteria (lowest is best)
r0$waic$waic; r1$waic$waic; r2$waic$waic; r3$waic$waic
r0$dic$dic; r1$dic$dic; r2$dic$dic; r3$dic$dic

# compare models with cross validation (lowest is best)
cval <- function(result=r1){
  test <- sum(result$cpo$failure)
  if(test != 0) print("some cpo estimates failed the quality test. do not use.")
  return(-2 * sum(log(result$cpo$cpo), na.rm = T))
}
cval(r0); cval(r1); cval(r2); cval(r3)

# pick a model and get credible intervals for fixed effects
r1$summary.fixed[,c(1,3,5)]

# get posterior probability that a parameter estimate is positive
1 - inla.pmarginal(0, r2$marginals.fixed$x2)

# get variation explained by random effects
brinla::bri.hyperpar.summary(r3)[, c(1,3,5)]

# look at model fit to data
hist(r1$cpo$pit) # should be uniformish
plot(r1$summary.fitted.values$mean, dat$y); abline(0,1)
# x values are posterior mean fitted values that include fixed and random effects
